description:
Why this issue exists: token_store.rs verify() fetches the stored token hash from SQLite using the hash of the presented token as the lookup key, then performs a subtle::ConstantTimeEq comparison between the stored hash and the presented hash. Since the SQL WHERE clause already selected by exact hash equality, if a row is returned the hashes are identical by database invariant. The CT comparison is redundant (though harmless).

What needs to be done: Remove the CT comparison — it provides no security benefit here because the database already performed an equality check. Add a comment explaining why CT comparison is not needed: the SQL lookup is keyed on the hash; if a row is returned, equality is guaranteed by the DB. Note: the existing subtle::ConstantTimeEq usage in the admin bearer token path (stoa admin servers) IS correct and should not be removed — this finding is specific to token_store.rs only.
title: idiom: token_store ct_eq comparison is redundant after hash-keyed SQL lookup
